topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: Assessment tasks follow transitional period frameworks: six Levels of AI Assistance (No Assistance, Simple Editing Assistance, Planning or Design Assistance, Assistance with Attribution, Generative AI Software-based Assessments, Not Applicable) apply to Term 3 2026, Semester 2 2026, and Hexamester 5 2026; three AI Assessment Modes (Can't Use AI, Can Use AI, Must Use AI) apply to Hexamester 6 2026 and Summer Term 2027. The future Assessment and Feedback Procedure is scheduled for phased rollout across Term 3 2027, Semester 2 2027, and Hexamester 1 2027 (with clauses taking effect in January 2027 and January 2028); current assessments must follow current period framework instructions.
topics.scope: Student Plagiarism Management Procedure; Assessment and Feedback Procedure; Information Governance Procedure; Library TDM Guidance. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.

claims.text: UNSW's student guidance lists six Levels of AI Assistance for Term 3 2026, Semester 2 2026 and Hexamester 5 2026: No Assistance, Simple Editing Assistance, Planning or Design Assistance, Assistance with Attribution, Generative AI Software-based Assessments, and Not Applicable. For Hexamester 6 2026 and Summer Term 2027, the page specifies three AI Assessment Modes: Can't Use AI, Can Use AI and Must Use AI. Students should use the framework for their teaching period and check each assessment's instructions.

evidence.quote:
The three AI assessment modes are:
Can’t Use AI – Independent Demonstration: AI is excluded where its use would undermine evidence of your independent knowledge, skills or judgement.
Can Use AI – Open Practice: AI may support your learning and task completion where its use does not undermine the evidence the assessment is intended to collect.
Must Use AI – AI Capability Demonstration: AI use is required where AI capability is itself part of the intended learning and you need to demonstrate that capability through the assessment.

evidence.quote:
The role of AI in your assessments
From Hexamester 6 2026 and Summer Term 2027, UNSW will transition from Levels of AI Assistance to a new framework for how you can use AI in your assessments: AI Assessment Modes.
As the role of AI in professional practice continues to change, your assessments are evolving to help you develop the skills to use AI effectively, critically and responsibly.
During the transition, make sure you refer to the framework that applies to your current teaching period. You can find information about how you can use AI in each specific assessment in your course outline and instructions from your lecturer or tutor.

claims.text: Under UNSW's 'No Assistance' level, students are not permitted to use any generative AI tools, software, or service to search for or generate information or answers.

evidence.quote: This assessment is designed for you to complete without the use of any generative AI.  You are not permitted to use any generative AI tools, software or service to search for or generate information or answers.
evidence.title: Using AI in university | Current Students – UNSW Sydney
evidence.location: Levels of AI assistance > No assistance

claims.text: UNSW requires that students must follow assessment instructions regarding AI use, that what students present must be their own work, and that students must acknowledge all sources including AI as an external source using proper referencing.

evidence.quote: Students must follow the assessment instructions... What students present must be their own work... Students must acknowledge sources. Students should attribute all sources using proper referencing, unless the assessment nature or instructions exempt them from doing so. External sources that must be referenced include both the work of others and sources from digital or physical objects, with AI classified as an external source.
evidence.title: Helping you guide your students | UNSW Staff Teaching Gateway
evidence.location: Section 'Guidance to students' > fundamental principles of assessment

claims.text: Under Section 6.1 of UNSW's Assessment and Feedback Procedure, the course outline will be published at least one week before the start of the teaching period and will specify for each assessment the allowed role of artificial intelligence and, where relevant, how it can be used. The procedure specifies phased applicability across teaching periods: effective generally from Term 3 2026, Semester 2 2026, and Hexamester 1 2027, with clauses 1.1–1.2 and 1.4 effective from 1 January 2027, and clauses 2.1–2.2 and 3.5–3.7 effective from 1 January 2028.

evidence.quote:
6.1.  The course outline will be published at least one week before the start of the teaching period and will include the following for each assessment:
purpose  learning outcomes  the allowed role of artificial intelligence and, where relevant, how it can be used  weighting toward the  course result   when the assessment task is due for submission and its submission instructions, or when the assessment task will be held  timing and type of feedback  whether it is a hurdle task  whether a short extension is available  whether a supplementary assessment is available.
evidence.title: Assessment and Feedback Procedure within the Assessment and Progression Policy hub
evidence.location: lines 248-249; Section 6. Communicating assessment expectations to students, Clause 6.1

evidence.quote:
Unless stated otherwise, this procedure is effective for all programs and courses within the scope of this policy from the following teaching periods :
Term 3, 2026  Semester 2, 2026  Hexamester 1, 2027.
The following requirements are effective from  1 January 2027 :
clauses 1.1 – 1.2 (aligning an assessment to PLOs, SLOs and CLOs)  clause 1.4 (assuring PLOs and SLOs with secure assessment).
The following requirements are effective from  1 January 2028 :
clauses 2.1 – 2.2 (program-level approaches to assessment)  clauses 3.5 – 3.7 (assessment workload).
evidence.title: Assessment and Feedback Procedure within the Assessment and Progression Policy hub
evidence.location: lines 192-197; Procedure Implementation & Version Control, Effective dates

topics.title: Privacy & sensitive data
topics.summary: UNSW's Information Governance Policy applies to students, researchers, research trainees, employees and affiliates; individual procedures may have narrower scope. Its AI procedure requires confidentiality of highly sensitive, sensitive, commercial and personal information and an AI self-assurance assessment before use, except for an approved, deployed enterprise-grade system such as Copilot. Student guidance separately advises against including personal or sensitive information in AI prompts.

additionalTopics.title: Academic integrity & procedures
additionalTopics.summary: UNSW manages academic integrity under the Student Plagiarism Management Procedure across five tiers: Poor scholarship, Minor, Moderate, Significant, and Serious. For Minor plagiarism, the rubric states that a mark reduction should not exceed 10% of the maximum grade available for the assessment task (from plagiarism rubric Appendix 3 footnote 4, not an absolute cap). School authorities manage Poor scholarship and Minor through Significant cases. Serious cases must be referred to the Conduct & Integrity Office (CIO) as potential student misconduct, with potential outcomes ranging from task/course failure to suspension or exclusion (not automatic penalties). Actions outside the outcomes available for a level require CIO approval, and repeated instances may also be escalated to student misconduct. For School-level outcomes notified under clause 4.3(a), an internal review request must be made within 20 business days of that notice and is limited to procedural fairness, not the merits. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process.
additionalTopics.scope: Student Plagiarism Management Procedure; Assessment and Feedback Procedure; Information Governance Procedure; Library TDM Guidance. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.

claims.text: UNSW's teacher guidance describes preliminary checks and consultation for suspected AI writing. Under the formal Student Plagiarism Management Procedure, the Course Authority or SSIA should notify the student in writing of detected Poor scholarship/Minor/Moderate/Significant plagiarism and proposed academic action; the student has 5 business days to respond. For these School-level outcomes, an internal review must be emailed to the Head of School or delegate within 20 business days of the Notification of Outcome under clause 4.3(a). Review is limited to procedural fairness, not the merits. The reviewer must not have participated in the initial decision; the student is to be notified of the review outcome within 10 business days of receipt of the review request. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process; these School-level deadlines must not be presented as deadlines for every serious-misconduct case.
